checks.claim: Perplexity mean within-language brand-set Jaccard = 68.2% vs mean cross-language = 44.5% (delta 23.8 points), pooled over 560 within pairs (28 per prompt per language) and 640 cross pairs (64 per prompt) across 10 prompts, with brand sets extracted from response.text via the lexicon.
checks.my_numbers: Independent script (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ifhambaig-aeoandgeo/bce92e9c-4e91-47fa-95b6-42dca4cbf2e6/scratchpad/verify_jaccard.py): mean within = 68.2112%, mean cross = 44.4576%, delta = 23.7537 points; n_within = 560 pairs, n_cross = 640 pairs. Per-prompt deltas (points): F01 9.07, F02 16.84, F03 26.52, F04 16.04, F05 36.79, S01 10.77, S02 6.44, S03 55.67, S04 7.14, S05 52.26. Per-prompt within/cross (%): F01 61.08/52.01, F02 80.87/64.03, F03 79.54/53.02, F04 82.47/66.43, F05 47.74/10.95, S01 75.36/64.58, S02 61.34/54.89, S03 76.13/20.46, S04 56.04/48.91, S05 61.54/9.28.
checks.discrepancies: None material. (1) The claimed delta 23.8 is the rounded unrounded-difference (23.75), not 68.2-44.5=23.7; this is standard practice, not an error. (2) Raw directory contains extra reps r9/r10 for four Perplexity cells (F02_en, F02_hg, S01_en, S01_hg); I used reps 1-8 only, matching the tidy dataset and the C(8,2) convention. (3) Matching-rule ambiguities are immaterial: matching bare case-sensitive "W" vs aliases-only changes nothing; applying Lee/Lee-Cooper longest-match-first shifts within to 68.01% and delta to 23.50, still rounding-consistent with the claim.

checks.claim: ChatGPT within-language brand-set Jaccard 54.2% vs cross-language 52.1% (delta 2.1 points), exact one-sided sign-flip permutation p=0.0352 over 10 per-prompt deltas (all 1024 sign assignments enumerated).
checks.my_numbers: Fully independent recomputation from data/raw/*_chatgpt_*.json + brand-lexicon.json (own script, analyze.mjs never opened). Using the balanced design of reps 1-8 per cell (8 en + 8 hg per prompt; within = 2*C(8,2) = 56 pairs/prompt, cross = 8*8 = 64 pairs/prompt; Jaccard both-empty=1, one-empty=0; word-boundary regex (?<![A-Za-z0-9])name(?![A-Za-z0-9]), case-insensitive except risky_alias entries matched case-sensitively, bare 'W' never matched per lexicon rule 5): pooled within = 0.541899 (54.19%), pooled cross = 0.520795 (52.08%), mean per-prompt delta = 0.02110 (2.11 points). Per-prompt deltas: F01 +0.0005, F02 -0.0080, F03 +0.0111, F04 -0.0005, F05 +0.0001, S01 +0.0500, S02 +0.0190, S03 +0.0947, S04 -0.0092, S05 +0.0532. Exact sign-flip permutation over all 2^10=1024 assignments: 36/1024 assignments have mean >= observed, one-sided p = 0.035156 = 0.0352. All three headline numbers match the claim exactly.
checks.discrepancies: None on the claim itself. Four notes from adversarial probing: (1) The raw directory is being appended to RIGHT NOW: a top-up job wrote r9/r10 files for F02 and S01 at 18:54-18:55 today (167->168 chatgpt files between two of my reads). Including those extra reps gives within 53.5%/cross 51.6% pooled (delta 2.02 pts) but the permutation count stays 36/1024 = 0.0352, so the finding survives; still, the published numbers correspond to the reps-1-8 snapshot and the paper should pin exactly which reps were analyzed before citing. (2) The test is one-sided as stated; the equivalent two-sided p is 72/1024 = 0.0703, which does not clear 0.05 - a citable writeup should keep the explicit one-sided framing (claim already does). (3) The effect is carried almost entirely by the saree/S prompts (S01, S03, S05); all five fashion F-prompt deltas are within +/-0.011, and 3 of 10 deltas are negative. (4) The risky_alias case-sensitivity rule is load-bearing in the conservative direction: matching risky aliases case-insensitively inflates the delta to 13.2 points (p=1/1024) via Hinglish false positives (bata/libas/soch/killer/mufti etc.), so the study's convention understates rather than manufactures the effect; Lee/Lee-Cooper suppression and bare-W handling change nothing.

checks.claim: The answer-language classifier (answerLanguage field in responses.json) is accurate; and Gemini answered 8 of 80 Hinglish prompts in Devanagari script.

Full-corpus label distribution: chatgpt/en 79 english + 1 hinglish; chatgpt/hg 80 hinglish; gemini/en 80 english; gemini/hg 71 hinglish + 8 hindi-devanagari + 1 english; perplexity/en 80 english; perplexity/hg 79 hinglish + 1 hindi-devanagari. Independent Devanagari script scan of all 480 raw texts: exactly 8 responses have >30% Devanagari letter share, all Gemini Hinglish cells (F01_hg_gemini_r2/r5/r6, F03_hg_gemini_r3, F05_hg_gemini_r1/r2/r7/r8), matching the 8 hindi-devanagari Gemini labels one-for-one; I read two in full and they are genuine Devanagari Hindi. Gemini 8/80 claim reproduced exactly.
checks.discrepancies: None within the 30-response stratified sample. Two issues found in adversarial spot-checks OUTSIDE the sample (among all 480): (1) S02_en_chatgpt_r8 is labeled "hinglish" but the full text is plain English with zero Hindi/Hinglish tokens (snippet: "If your priority is high protection + no obvious white cast on Indian skin, my first pick would be... If you tell me your skin type (oily/dry/combination) and roughly your skin tone (fair/medium/wheatish/deep)...") — a clear misclassification, possibly triggered by the word "wheatish" or brand names. (2) F02_hg_perplexity_r5 is labeled "hindi-devanagari" but is mixed-script, only ~12% Devanagari characters (starts "3000 रुपये के अंदर running shoes लेते समय..." then shifts largely to Roman Hinglish, e.g. "Kya dekhna chahiye purchase karte waqt"); "hinglish"/mixed would be arguably more accurate, so the corpus-wide hindi-devanagari total of 9 (8 Gemini + this 1 Perplexity) includes one borderline case. The Gemini 8/80 figure itself is unaffected.

checks.claim: Risky-alias brand matches (26 lexicon entries flagged risky_alias, matched case-sensitively with word boundaries) are genuine brand mentions and do not materially contaminate the study's headline metrics.
checks.my_numbers: Audited all 26 risky_alias brands: 802 (response,brand) risky pairs total; 307 pairs judged by eye from raw-text contexts plus full-population automated sweeps for Simple, Lee, Plum, W, Asian and next-word scans for all brands. False positives found: Simple 18/51 responses (35.3% FP; e.g. "Simple rule:", "Simple choice:", "H&M — Simple & modern", "Simple wedding-guest sarees"; 14 of 18 FPs in Hinglish responses, 6 reach top3Brands, 1 is firstBrand); Lee 3/26 (11.5%; text contains only "Lee Cooper" yet tagged both Lee and Lee Cooper: F01_en_gemini_r4, F01_hg_perplexity_r6, F01_hg_perplexity_r8); Asian 1/4 (25%; "Asian skin tones" in citation anchor, S02_en_gemini_r2 — and that phantom is firstBrand + top3). All other 23 risky brands: 0 FP in samples (fully sampled for 15 brands; 13-20 sampled for the rest), backed by full-population checks (all 89 Plum responses have a non-Kakadu-Plum brand mention; all 48 W responses contain "W for Woman/Women"). Overall: 22 FP pairs = 2.7% of risky pairs = 0.9% of all 2,435 brand pairs in responses.json.
checks.discrepancies: Three defects: (1) "Simple" is materially contaminated — 35% of its tagged responses are phantom (generic adjective/section headers), overstating Simple's visibility (51 vs true 33) and skewed 14:4 toward Hinglish responses, which biases any EN-vs-Hinglish comparison involving Simple and marginally deflates Hinglish indiaOriginShare (Simple is non-India); 6 phantoms reach top3Brands and 1 is firstBrand, so position-weighted metrics are also touched. (2) Lee/Lee Cooper longest-match-first resolution promised in lexicon rule notes is not enforced: 3 responses mentioning only Lee Cooper are double-tagged with Lee. (3) One phantom "Asian" (from a URL-encoded citation fragment "Asian skin tones") is that response's firstBrand. The other 23 risky brands, including feared cases Plum/Bata/Mufti/Killer/Libas/Soch/Roadster/Campus/Arrow, are clean — case-sensitive matching does its job.

India-origin share (mean of per-response india fraction; responses with zero matched brands excluded): chatgpt EN 0.744259 n=79 (1 zero-brand), HG 0.734366 n=78 (2 zero-brand); gemini EN 0.756570 n=79 (1 zero-brand), HG 0.820159 n=80; perplexity EN 0.635382 n=80, HG 0.651339 n=80 — all match claimed values to 6 decimals and claimed n exactly. Nykaa in-text ((?<![A-Za-z0-9])nykaa(?![A-Za-z0-9]) case-insensitive): chatgpt EN 8/80=0.1000, HG 6/80=0.0750; gemini EN 26/80=0.3250, HG 16/80=0.2000; perplexity EN 2/80=0.0250, HG 2/80=0.0250 — all exact matches, Wilson 95% CIs also reproduce (e.g. chatgpt EN [0.051547, 0.185109]). checks.discrepancies: Two notes, neither an error in the reported numbers. (1) Gemini citation rate depends on the URL-matching convention: 3 gemini responses (S02_en_gemini_r2 partially, S02_en_gemini_r3, S03_en_gemini_r7, S01_hg_gemini_r4) cite reddit.com/medium.com/makeupholicworld.com/blog.flash.co pages whose #:~:text= scroll-to-text fragments contain the word Nykaa; a naive 'URL contains nykaa' rule counts these and gives EN 17/80 (0.2125) and HG 7/80 (0.0875) instead of the reported 0.1875/0.075. The reported figures correspond to matching the cited host (nykaa.com, nykaafashion.com, nykaaman.com), which is the more defensible definition of 'cites Nykaa'; the study should state this convention explicitly since the literal substring reading gives different numbers. (2) The raw directory holds 496 files: F02 and S01 cells have extra r9/r10 reps (9-10 reps in 11 engine/lang cells). The analysis uses only r1-r8 (480 responses, 80 per engine/lang cell); the exclusion is consistent and reproduces all n's, but the study should document why the extra reps exist and that they were excluded.

synthesis:
HINGLISH GEO STUDY - VERIFICATION SYNTHESIS

Six independent checks. All six reproduced. Zero REFUTED. Four carry notes that require action before publication.

PER-CHECK RESULTS

1. gemini-citations: CONFIRMED-WITH-NOTES. EN 72/80 = 90.0% with >=1 citation (mean 9.4) vs Hinglish 33/80 = 41.3% (mean 5.2); all four numbers match exactly on the reps 1-8 snapshot. Note: a top-up run is appending r9/r10 files for F02/S01 right now; recounting over all files present shifts to EN 90.5%, HG 40.5% (same conclusion, different denominators).

2. perplexity-jaccard: CONFIRMED (cleanest check). Within-language 68.21% vs cross-language 44.46%, delta 23.75 points, over 560 within / 640 cross pairs. Delta of 23.8 is the correctly rounded unrounded difference. Robust to matching-rule variants (worst case 23.50).

3. chatgpt-smallest: CONFIRMED-WITH-NOTES. Within 54.19% vs cross 52.08%, delta 2.11 points, exact one-sided permutation p = 36/1024 = 0.0352; all three headline numbers match. Fragility notes: two-sided p = 0.0703 does not clear 0.05, so the one-sided framing must stay explicit; the effect is carried almost entirely by S01/S03/S05 (all five F-prompt deltas within +/-0.011, 3 of 10 deltas negative); including the incoming r9/r10 reps shifts pooled values slightly (delta 2.02) but p stays 0.0352.

4. answer-language: CONFIRMED-WITH-NOTES. 30/30 agreement on the stratified sample; Gemini 8/80 Devanagari reproduced one-for-one via independent script scan. Two label errors found outside the sample: S02_en_chatgpt_r8 labeled hinglish but is plain English, and F02_hg_perplexity_r5 labeled hindi-devanagari but is only ~12% Devanagari mixed-script. Corpus-wide devanagari total of 9 includes one borderline case; the 8/80 Gemini figure is unaffected.

5. risky-alias-audit: CONFIRMED-WITH-NOTES, but this is the most material finding. Overall contamination is low (22 FP pairs = 0.9% of all 2,435 brand pairs), and 23 of 26 risky brands are clean. Three defects: (a) "Simple" is 35.3% phantom (18/51 responses; true visibility 33, not 51), skewed 14:4 toward Hinglish, with 6 phantoms in top3Brands and 1 as firstBrand; (b) Lee/Lee Cooper longest-match-first is promised in the lexicon but not enforced (3 responses double-tagged); (c) one phantom "Asian" (citation-anchor text) is a response's firstBrand.

6. india-share-and-nykaa: CONFIRMED-WITH-NOTES. All six India-origin shares match to 6 decimals with exact n's; all Nykaa in-text and citation rates match exactly, including Wilson CIs. Note: the Gemini citation figures (EN 18.75%, HG 7.5%) depend on hostname-based matching; a literal URL-substring rule gives 21.25%/8.75% because of #:~:text= fragments containing "nykaa". The reported convention is the more defensible one but must be stated.

OVERALL ASSESSMENT

The headline claims are safe to publish. Every reported number was independently reproduced exactly, including the two effect-size claims (Gemini citation gap, Perplexity consistency gap), the marginal ChatGPT result, and all RQ1 shares. Nothing was refuted and no reported figure is wrong as stated.

Required changes before publication (all fixable without altering headline conclusions):

1. Freeze the dataset. A top-up run is actively writing r9/r10 reps for F02 and S01 into data/raw/ after responses.json was generated. Either stop the run and pin the analysis explicitly to reps 1-8 (documenting why the extra reps exist and are excluded), or wait for it to finish and regenerate every number. Do not publish against a moving directory.

2. Fix the "Simple" lexicon entry (require context or drop the bare-word alias) and regenerate visibility, top3, firstBrand, and indiaOriginShare figures. The 14:4 Hinglish skew of its phantoms directly biases the study's central EN-vs-Hinglish comparison for that brand and marginally deflates Hinglish India-origin share.

3. Enforce Lee/Lee Cooper longest-match-first as the lexicon notes promise (3 affected responses), and fix the phantom "Asian" firstBrand in S02_en_gemini_r2.

4. Correct or caveat the two answer-language labels (S02_en_chatgpt_r8, F02_hg_perplexity_r5) and state the corpus-wide devanagari count as 8 clear + 1 borderline.

5. State two methodological conventions explicitly in the writeup: the ChatGPT permutation test is one-sided (two-sided would not reach 0.05), and Gemini "cites Nykaa" means the cited hostname is a Nykaa property, not URL-substring matching.

6. Add a robustness caveat to the ChatGPT finding: the effect is concentrated in the saree prompts; frame it as suggestive and category-driven rather than uniform.

With items 1 and 2 addressed, all six checks support publication.
